analysis:
This PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. It bumps the last-updated date and revises the GLM5Next video paragraph. Frame i is now timed at i / nominalFrameRate, and variable-frame-rate video is indexed instead of refused with a deterministic 400. The "Processor refusals" sentence is updated to match. No executable code, auth, attestation, encryption, billing, or key-handling paths change in the supplied evidence.

Relevant threat IDs: T-050 (video plaintext temp files) and T-007/T-056 (correctness claims). The doc says VFR is no longer refused. The actual loader change is outside the supplied batch, so the docs/implementation match cannot be verified here. The doc still describes bounded resources: 2 FPS sampling, the 512 MiB decoded-frame cap, the 28,532 visual-token cap, and the VisionMemoryGate reservation with the video token ceiling. The decoded-frame cap bounds the memory impact. Reading VFR tracks frame by frame in presentation order, with timestamps from the average frame rate, could change timestamp text and sampling but not trust boundaries. The unreviewed concern is availability. An adversarial consumer could submit a pathological VFR video (huge frame count or extreme timestamps) that costs CPU or decode time before the cap triggers. The caps appear to apply, but that code is not supplied, so I record this as an integration question rather than a finding.

No threat-model assumption is invalidated by the documentation text. The remaining docs content (the prefix-cache, MTP, deadline, and calibration descriptions) is unchanged context. It remains consistent with T-041 (30-minute TTL, HMAC-keyed SSD tier) as far as it is described here.
